discussion_comments.comment_body: Intentional tradeoff. Before this change, a timed-out command whose `ProxyCommand`/`ProxyJump` descendant outlived `ssh` blocked its caller in `join()` until that descendant exited. That held up `machine add`, and for `connect_saved_ssh` it kept the reconnect worker from retrying. Now the caller returns at the timeout, and the two detached readers live exactly as long as the descendant holds the pipes. Typical proxies (`ssh -W`, `nc`, `coder ssh --stdio`) exit on stdin EOF once `ssh` is killed. Bounding this further would mean spawning `ssh` as its own process group and killing the group on timeout. That is platform-specific and changes every noninteractive caller, so I kept it out of this fix. Happy to add it if you prefer.
fixed in e53159dc: an interrupted send now stops at the shared deadline, covered by interrupted_sends_stop_at_the_deadline and an_interrupted_send_is_retried_before_the_deadline

Fixed. pane.send_input, agent.start and agent.prompt now share 64 completion-waiter permits across the app. A permit must be acquired before spawning, reserving a name or queuing bytes, and stays owned by the worker until it exits. Capacity and spawn failures return an error without sending input. Tests cover exhaustion, zero side effects, permit return and successful retry.

This bounds the input-completion resources introduced here; it does not claim to change the API listener's pre-existing connection-thread model.

Reviewed against 6cba6c647b8d4774a5d52a57e8dcb2e1b9d11e4c.

Addressed in 6eef9b18. Saved-membership checks now run independently of the Git cache refresh, using a one-shot queue with at most four detached workers. The regression keeps the first checkout's Git config blocked and verifies that a healthy saved membership completes validation and can answer `worktree.list`.

Workers remain bounded: a permanently stalled read retains its slot, without spawning replacements on refresh ticks. The existing optional Git status cache remains serialized, as documented in the PR.

Intentional tradeoff, not changing. Skipping environment reads for identified agents on WSL is the safety policy from #2179 that this PR was asked to adopt: reading `/proc/<pid>/environ` enters `access_remote_vm`, and on WSL that has been observed to block indefinitely while a multithreaded agent was exiting. A process-state check alone races with the stall, so the name check is deliberately conservative. The cost is that on WSL agent activations are not captured; the alternative is a main-loop stall during session save. Capturing the environment at agent launch instead would be a separate change.

Disposition: existing blocking-I/O limitation; no regression introduced by this slice.

On the PR base, [the input forwarder holds the acceptance mutex through Enter's write_submission_part](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/d6b40d4edd550ccea081f089605a64314f8c8b27/src/pty/actor.rs#L354-L362), and [that helper blocks on writer completion](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/d6b40d4edd550ccea081f089605a64314f8c8b27/src/pty/actor.rs#L376-L393). [Shutdown takes the same mutex](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/d6b40d4edd550ccea081f089605a64314f8c8b27/src/pty/actor.rs#L178-L183) before [PaneRuntime terminates the child](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/d6b40d4edd550ccea081f089605a64314f8c8b27/src/pane.rs#L1558-L1573). Thus an Enter write that never returns already blocks shutdown on the base.

The explicit per-Enter completion preserves this flush-before-teardown boundary while the forwarding task awaits asynchronously. Releasing the gate before waiting would let a second concurrent shutdown see no completion and close the master/terminate the child before the first Enter flush finishes. Tests cover this wait boundary and writer success/failure/discard releasing it. Bounded writer cancellation is separate behavior/design work; this PR intentionally preserves the existing contract.

Fixed in befecffe: shutdown now recovers the state mutex using the same pattern as the other actor transitions, preserves Released, and wakes paused workers. The canonical shutdown regression now poisons that mutex; it failed before the fix and passes afterward.

the 250 ms exit deadline intentionally bounds shutdown, including when a peer cannot drain a large paste in time. the old test required 1 mb to drain within that deadline and failed on macos. the tests now separately check registry input-before-detach ordering, complete large-frame flushing, and cancellation with a stalled peer. guaranteeing a complete arbitrarily large queue within the exit deadline is not the transport contract.

Fixed in `f68f24b1`. Unix now defers the handoff acknowledgement while an accepted submission is active, continues the bounded submission, then drains queued input and quiesces. A timed-out handoff rollback clears the deferred request. The backpressure test now verifies that handoff waits and succeeds instead of returning `WouldBlock`.

Fixed in 063c484e at the owning public gate. `begin_handoff` now returns `WouldBlock` before enqueueing a second control command when handoff has already disabled user writes, so no later request can overwrite `pending_handoff` or roll back the first request. The existing handoff/quiesce test now verifies a second start is rejected and the first handoff remains quiesced.
Fixed in 4b06a614: the readiness handshake now uses a two-second `recv_timeout` and returns a timed-out error instead of blocking client notification handling indefinitely.
